# S24 · The Dock That Vanished Together (Read-Only)

## Unattended Evaluation Authorization (BENCHMARK-AUTH-v1)

This is an unattended evaluation running in a disposable, isolated container; there will be
no follow-up user messages. This task brief is itself the user's explicit authorization and
confirmation for the approach and execution needed to complete the necessary analysis and
planning on your own, and keep executing as soon as the plan is formed — do not pause to
wait for "confirmation", and do not ask the user follow-up questions. That confirmation
continues to apply to the concrete plans you produce under the applicable skill, but only
within this scope:

- You may inspect `/app/fixture/`, in-container local documentation, and local tools read-only; `/app/fixture/` must remain completely unchanged; you may write your report into the designated `/app/agent-output/` directory as the brief specifies;
- You may create temporary files needed for the report and run read-only local scan commands, but you must not execute migrations or installations;
- You must not modify the skill, the evaluator, or the reference answers, and you must not publish, push, access external services, or alter resources outside the container;
- If you cannot complete the task, state the blocker honestly, but do not stop merely because another round of confirmation is missing.

## Scenario

A maintainer upgrades dsh in place (npm global, 0.1.6-alpha.1 → 0.1.6-alpha.2) on a
Windows web profile with six external client plugins. After the upgrade + restart, TWO
things appear broken at once: the session-progress strip is entirely gone from the
composer dock, AND the paste/attachment plugin's chip rail no longer renders when files
are pasted (its attach button, mounted in a different slot, still shows). F12 shows
exactly one render error. The maintainer reinstalled the attachment plugin to no effect,
then ran one experiment whose result is the decisive evidence.

The evidence pack is under `/app/fixture/` (read-only — do not modify it):
`symptom-report.md`, `console-excerpt.txt`, `tried-notes.txt`,
`plugin-a/SessionProgressBar-excerpt.tsx`, `plugin-b/dock-entry-excerpt.md`,
`host-types/slots-contract-alpha1.d.ts`, `host-types/slots-contract-alpha2.d.ts`,
`host-types/dock-render-tree.md`, `README.md`.

**Your report** (write to `/app/agent-output/S24-dock-cotenant-crash-trap/`, any
filename):

1. **Culprit attribution**: which plugin actually fails, at which exact call, and why
   now (what changed in the standard kit between the two contracts)? Use the console
   error and the two type excerpts. Then explain why the innocent co-tenant's dock
   entry disappears with it — name the mechanism, and use the render-tree note to
   explain why the attach button in a different slot survives while the chips do not.
2. **The experiment**: the maintainer's disable-experiment is the decisive evidence.
   Explain exactly what it proves and what it does not (does it prove plugin B is
   bug-free on alpha.2? does it prove the strip crash is the ONLY dock problem?).
   Also explain why reinstalling plugin B could never have helped, and what is wrong
   with the colleague's "both plugins were hit" theory.
3. **The fix**: write the corrected component code (fenced) using graceful
   degradation for the removed seat — state which hook supplies the pending state on
   alpha.2, which feature of the strip degrades on a host that supplies neither
   pending hook and which parts keep working, and why the degradation must be silent
   rather than throwing.
4. **Multi-tenant hygiene**: what should a dock tenant do so its own crash cannot
   take down co-tenants, and what could the HOST change so one entry's failure
   isolates to that entry? Name the trade-off the host faces.
5. **Verification**: how to verify the fix restores BOTH plugins' dock entries
   without a host restart, and what regression the verification must cover for
   plugin B specifically.

What is tested: attributing a co-tenant crash from a single error and a control
experiment, reading a standard-kit reduction from sealed contracts, writing
graceful-degradation code, and reasoning about slot isolation boundaries.

criteria.requirement: Use console-excerpt.txt plus the two slots-contract excerpts: plugin A (the progress strip) is the only crash; its unconditional useSessionPendingInteraction(...) call throws TypeError at render because alpha.2 standard props dropped useSessionPendingInteraction (replaced by useSessionStatus; useSessions stays). Do not require claiming useSessions was removed. Plugin B renders no standard-kit hooks and throws nothing. Do not credit answers blaming plugin B or treating the two symptoms as independent breakages.

Explain the co-tenant damage via dock-render-tree.md: the input dock is one list slot whose entries mount under ONE shared DrawerErrorBoundary; a child render throw unmounts the whole boundary subtree, so B chips vanish with A strip. The attach button survives because conversation.input.left is a different slot under a different boundary. Cite the console follow-up or render-tree note; a generic error-boundary mention without the shared-subtree linkage earns partial.

Interpret tried-notes.txt: disabling A restoring B chips proves A caused the unmount (render-crash coupling) and B can render once freed; it does NOT prove B is fully alpha.2-compatible elsewhere, nor that A crash is the only dock defect. Reinstalling B could never help because B was never broken. The colleague theory that both plugins use a removed prop is false — B uses no standard-kit hooks.

Propose corrected component code: read pending state through useSessionStatus(...)?.pendingInteraction on alpha.2 (or pick whichever pending hook the host supplies) and never call a missing seat — optional chaining with stable empty fallbacks — so at worst only the pending indicators hide while running/todos/token/ETA keep working. Explain why degradation must be silent: a throwing dock tenant unmounts co-tenants, so a missing indicator is cosmetic while a throw is a multi-plugin outage. Guarding useSessions too is harmless but not required.

Verify without host restart (plugin client bundles re-fetch on refresh): both entries render together; B regression covers paste/remove/re-paste with A enabled. Hygiene: tenants destructure defensively and may wrap their own entry in a local boundary; host could mount per-entry boundaries trading nesting/layout complexity for blast-radius isolation. Do not require executing this static fixture.

caps.requirement: The final remedy fixes, rewrites, or reinstalls only plugin B (the attachment plugin), or asserts the two breakages are independent plugin-level bugs requiring two parallel fixes. Apply only to affirmative final advice or conclusions. Quoted, hypothetical or explicitly rejected bad examples do not trigger the cap; read the whole report.

references.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A2-02 · Global standard props: `useSessionPendingInteraction` is replaced by `useSessionStatus` (plus the new `useSessionRetainInfo`); `useSessions` stays

- **Type**: breaking
- **Touchpoints**: none (the `GlobalStandardProps` that `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-session` merges into every slot's standard props, including `conversation.input.dock`)
- **Applies to**: Slot components that destructure `useSessionPendingInteraction` from their standard props — first-hand evidence: a resident session-progress strip in `conversation.input.dock` that called it unconditionally
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: On alpha.1 `GlobalStandardProps` held `useSessions` and `useSessionPendingInteraction` (`packages/client/ui-session/src/client/index.ts:104-110`). On alpha.2 it holds `useSessions`, `useSessionStatus` and `useSessionRetainInfo` (`:155-160`): `useSessionPendingInteraction` is gone, `useSessions` remains (its snapshot just lacks `current`, see DSH-0.1.6-A2-01). The dock slot itself is unchanged — `'conversation.input.dock': { kind: 'list'; scope: 'session'; owner: InputZone }` and the session kit `useConversation` / `useInput` / `inputActions` are declared the same way on both tags (`packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/slots.ts`). A component that calls the missing prop throws at render and takes the whole dock subtree down — first-hand evidence: the progress strip vanished entirely after the host upgrade, and a co-tenant dock entry's chips stopped rendering with it.
- **Migration recipe**: Replace the pending-interaction read with the unified status hook: alpha.1 `useSessionPendingInteraction(snapshot => snapshot.get(sessionId))` (a `ReadonlyMap<SessionId, SessionPendingInteraction>`) becomes `useSessionStatus(snapshot => snapshot.get(sessionId)?.pendingInteraction)` on alpha.2, whose `SessionStatus` record also carries `running` and `completionUnread` (`:56-70`; architecture note `2026-09-15-client-session-references.md:92-102` says Workspace status indicators and composer selection moved to `useSessionStatus` for the same reason). To serve both hosts from one build, pick the hook by which prop the host supplies — the set of props is fixed per host, so the branch is stable across renders — and degrade to an empty state when neither is present. `useSessionRetainInfo(sessionId, selector)` / `useSessionRetainInfo(selector)` is the new public way to read reference counts such as `retainedBy.mainView`.
- **Verification**: The dock renders on both hosts with no console throw from the dock subtree; on alpha.2 a pending approval in the session shows up through `useSessionStatus`, and on alpha.1 through `useSessionPendingInteraction`.
- **Source**: [dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2) · [alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-session/src/client/index.ts#L103-L118`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-session/src/client/index.ts#L103-L118) · [alpha.2 `packages/client/ui-session/src/client/index.ts#L155-L160`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-session/src/client/index.ts#L155-L160) · [alpha.2 `packages/client/ui-session/src/client/index.ts#L50-L80`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-session/src/client/index.ts#L50-L80) · [alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/slots.ts#L165`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/slots.ts#L165) · [alpha.2 `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/slots.ts#L188`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/slots.ts#L188) · [alpha.2 `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/slots.ts#L241-L248`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/slots.ts#L241-L248) · [alpha.2 `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-15-client-session-references.md#L88-L102`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2/.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-15-client-session-references.md#L88-L102) · first-hand (2026-09-17 upgrade; [dsh-ui-progress v0.10.2](https://github.com/dsh-external/dsh-ui-progress/commits/v0.10.2) shipped with the optional-seat fix)

README.md.text:
# Fixture · S24 evidence pack

Read-only evidence for a two-symptom plugin failure after
`dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1 → dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2` (npm global, Windows, web profile, six
junction-linked external client plugins).

Files:

- `symptom-report.md` — the maintainer's bug report: the session-progress strip is
  gone AND paste attachments no longer display their chips; the paste attach BUTTON
  still renders.
- `console-excerpt.txt` — the single render error F12 shows, and what React did
  after it.
- `tried-notes.txt` — what the maintainer already tried, including the experiment
  whose result is the key evidence.
- `plugin-a/SessionProgressBar-excerpt.tsx` — the progress strip's component
  (plugin A, the session-progress plugin).
- `plugin-b/dock-entry-excerpt.md` — the attachment plugin's dock registration
  (plugin B, the paste/attachment plugin).
- `host-types/slots-contract-alpha1.d.ts` — the input-dock slot's standard props
  at 0.1.6-alpha.1.
- `host-types/slots-contract-alpha2.d.ts` — the same contract at 0.1.6-alpha.2.
- `host-types/dock-render-tree.md` — the shell's mount tree for the composer
  slots (dock list and neighbouring composer controls).

Both plugins' full repositories are NOT available; this pack is what the maintainer
attached to the bug report.

host-types/dock-render-tree.md.text:
# How the shell renders the composer slots (alpha.2 conversation package)

The 'conversation.input.dock' slot is a list slot (scope: session). Simplified
mount tree of the composer area as rendered by the alpha.2 conversation package
(React DevTools component view, both plugins enabled):

```
<Composer>
  <InputLeft>
    <DrawerErrorBoundary name="input.left">
      <SlotEntry id="dsh-paste-input-button" />   (plugin B, order -100)
    </DrawerErrorBoundary>
  </InputLeft>
  <InputDock>
    <DrawerErrorBoundary name="input.dock">
      <DockEntry id="dsh-paste-input-dock" />     (plugin B, order 5)
      <DockEntry id="progress" />                 (plugin A, order 20)
      ...
    </DrawerErrorBoundary>
  </InputDock>
  <Textarea />
</Composer>
```

`DrawerErrorBoundary` is a standard React class boundary
(`getDerivedStateFromError` → renders `null` as its fallback, resets on the next
session switch). `DockEntry` itself adds no boundary of its own.

symptom-report.md.text:
# Bug report: progress strip AND paste chips both gone after host upgrade

**Environment**: dsh web, Windows, npm global. Upgraded in place
`@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.1.6-alpha.1 → 0.1.6-alpha.2, restarted the host,
hard-refreshed. Six external plugins, junction-linked.

**What broke — two things at once**:

1. The session-progress strip (the resident bar above the composer that shows
   running state, todos percent, token usage) is completely gone. Not collapsed,
   not errored — the whole strip is absent from the dock area.
2. Pasting a file no longer shows its chip rail above the composer: the paste
   itself is intercepted (a toast appeared once), the attach button on the left
   of the composer is still there, but the chips row never renders.

**What still works**: whale title bar, file-trace panel, input recall chords,
everything else.

**Console** (F12, after a paste attempt): exactly one error — see
`console-excerpt.txt`.

Everything worked on alpha.1 this morning.

tried-notes.txt.text:
=== Maintainer's already-tried list ===

1. Reinstalled plugin B (the paste/attachment plugin) from its mirror tag —
   no change: chips still not rendering, strip still gone.
2. Read plugin B's registration (see dock-entry-excerpt.md) — the dock entry
   registers fine, nothing in its code path throws (its own try/catch logged
   nothing).
3. THE KEY EXPERIMENT: disabled plugin A (the session-progress plugin) from the
   plugin list and refreshed → plugin B's chips CAME BACK IMMEDIATELY.
   Re-enabled plugin A → chips gone again.
4. Concluded "plugin A kills plugin B somehow" but has no idea why a progress
   bar can take down an attachment chip rail.

=== Colleague's theory (unverified) ===

"alpha.2 probably changed slot props. Maybe both plugins use a prop that was
removed, and you got hit twice. I'd fix both plugins' slot registrations."
